name: user_graph
summary: XMLParser-shaped graph over the user's chain of thought. Each chat turn lands as a <turn> element with attributes (uuid, user, turn_idx, timestamp, chain_crystal, tier) and child nodes (words, prompt, produced_chain, forward_chain, ngrams). predict_next(words, k) finds past turns whose n-grams overlap the incoming words.
engine_pattern: extends ParserCursor (XMLParser API). Writer appends turns + ngrams + edges to the JSONL document.
node_kinds_written: element name='root' depth=0 (seeded on first open)
element name='turn' depth=1 (one per chat turn; attributes carry identity + crystal backlink)
text name='words' depth=2 (the user's raw input)
text name='produced_chain' depth=2 (the master workspace chain this turn produced)
text name='forward_chain' depth=2 (the projected forward chain for this turn)
element name='ngram' depth=2 (one per extracted n-gram, attributes: hash + size)
ngram_strategy: word-level 2-grams + 3-grams via _WORD_RE. Lowercased. Each grams hash is blake3-truncated to 16 chars. Shared with moe_router (same hash → same key across substrates).

inbound_callers: CLI: python3 user_graph.py record | predict | walk | ngrams
routing_connections.substrate_writes: ~/.cc/user_graph.jsonl (record_turn appends ~N+5 lines per turn where N = ngram count)

predict_next_algorithm: 1) extract_ngrams(words) → list of (gram, hash). 2) for each hash, look up ngram_to_turns. 3) score each past turn by # of matching hashes. 4) sort by (-score, turn_uuid) for deterministic ranking. 5) return top-k Predictions with words, prompt, forward_chain, tier, timestamp, chain_crystal.
guarantees: Append-only — every event is a new JSONL line; turns and edges never overwritten
Deterministic — same JSONL bytes → same UserGraphIndex → same predictions
Cross-substrate linked — every turn carries chain_crystal pointing to its inference_logger record
Walkable as XML — `python3 user_graph.py walk` dumps the entire structure with depths + offsets
Ngram hash matches moe_router's hash (same algorithm) — joinable across substrates
usage_example:
from user_graph import UserGraph, UserGraphIndex
g = UserGraph(); g.open()
idx = UserGraphIndex.build_from(g)
for p in idx.predict_next('build the forward projector', k=3):
    print(p.score, p.words, p.forward_chain[:80])
